title: DomusFM: A Foundation Model for Event-Based Behavioral Monitoring in Smart-Homes
abstract: arXiv:2602.01910v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Smart-home sensor-based behavioral monitoring holds significant potential for healthcare, independent living, and early detection of functional or cognitive changes. In this setting, tasks like activity recognition, prediction, and pattern discovery provide complementary views of daily life, supporting the modeling of personal routines and habits, and their long-term changes. Existing approaches, however, face critical limitations. Supervised approaches require impractical amounts of labeled activity data to capture the variability of daily behavior across residents and environments. Foundation models represent a promising direction for learning transferable representations of latent behavioral patterns from sensor data. Still, current efforts are mostly designed for continuous inertial or physiological sensor data and do not address the sparse, discrete, and semantically rich event streams produced by smart homes. translated_title: DomusFM：智能家居中基于事件的居家行为监测的基础模型
translated_abstract: 基于智能家居传感器的行为监测在医疗保健、独立生活以及早期发现功能或认知变化方面具有巨大潜力。在此背景下，活动识别、预测和模式发现等任务为日常生活提供了互补视角，支持对个人常规习惯及其长期变化的建模。然而，现有方法面临关键限制。监督方法需要不切实际的大量标注活动数据，以捕捉不同居民和环境间日常行为的变异性。基础模型是学习从传感器数据中潜在行为模式的可迁移表示的有前景方向，但当前工作大多针对连续的惯性或生理传感器数据设计，未能处理智能家居产生的稀疏、离散且语义丰富的事件流。在本文中，我们提出DomusFM，一个专门为智能家居事件流定制的基于事件的基础模型，通过预训练和微调策略实现行为监测任务的有效表示学习。
tldr: 本文提出DomusFM，这是首个专门针对智能家居稀疏事件流设计的基础模型，通过预训练和微调实现行为监测任务的可迁移表示学习，克服了传统监督方法对大量标注数据的依赖。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DomusFM, the first foundation model tailored for sparse event streams in smart homes, enabling transferable representation learning for behavioral monitoring via pretraining and fine-tuning, overcoming reliance on extensive labeled data.
